chmmc-2012-fall-power-01b.prompt: Notation: $\sum_{i=a}^bk_i$ is the sum and $\prod_{i=a}^bk_i$ the product of the numbers $k_i$ for $i$ from $a$ to $b$. For $n\ge1$ let $$S_n=\left(\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{2^i-1}{2^i}\right)\cdot\left(1+\sum_{i=1}^n\left(2^{-i}\cdot\prod_{j=1}^i\frac{2^j}{2^j-1}\right)\right).$$ Find a recurrence relation, writing $S_{n+1}$ in terms of $S_n$.

chmmc-2012-fall-power-01c.prompt: Notation: $\sum_{i=a}^bk_i$ is the sum and $\prod_{i=a}^bk_i$ the product of the numbers $k_i$ for $i$ from $a$ to $b$. For $n\ge1$ let $$S_n=\left(\prod_{i=1}^n\frac{2^i-1}{2^i}\right)\cdot\left(1+\sum_{i=1}^n\left(2^{-i}\cdot\prod_{j=1}^i\frac{2^j}{2^j-1}\right)\right).$$ Given that $\prod_{i=1}^\infty\frac{2^i-1}{2^i}\ne0$, show by induction that $$\left(\prod_{i=1}^\infty\frac{2^i-1}{2^i}\right)\cdot\left(1+\sum_{i=1}^\infty\left(2^{-i}\cdot\prod_{j=1}^i\frac{2^j}{2^j-1}\right)\right)=1.$$ (You may use the recurrence $S_{n+1}=\frac{2^{n+1}-1}{2^{n+1}}S_n+2^{-(n+1)}$.)
chmmc-2012-fall-power-01c.answer: The infinite product times the infinite bracket equals 1 (proof)

chmmc-2012-fall-power-02a.prompt: Define $\binom nk$ as the number of ways to choose $k$ things out of $n$ choices. Give a combinatorial proof (without any algebra) that $$\binom nk=\binom{n-1}k+\binom{n-1}{k-1}.$$ (A combinatorial proof counts the same quantity in two ways.)
chmmc-2012-fall-power-02a.answer: Count $k$-subsets of an $n$-set by whether they contain a fixed element
